playbook:
When told the standing order target, I fire at that named live station unless the named station is Harbor (I never fire on Harbor).

When I fire, I choose a firing cell that balances probability and unpredictability: avoid repeating the same cell every round; cycle among a short set of cells and shift if opponents show a pattern.

When I receive the private shot result from the office, I file the public claim exactly the same (truthful claims only).

When I hide, I avoid predictable central-only hiding: vary between center and off-center cells and change after any round I am hit or after two rounds without being hit.

When posting a station note, use it to coordinate a reciprocal escort or to signal continuity ("steady on station") — be brief and credible so other captains can respond.

When I want escort points, I propose a mutual escort in my note naming a live boat; if they accept by naming me back, I file the reciprocal escort claim to secure the 5-point payout. Do not attempt to claim escort with names that are not actual boats.

When choosing an escort claim, only name one of the live boats in play or claim none; do not name non-boat entities.

When an opponent repeatedly targets my usual hides, change hiding pattern away from those cells; do not keep hiding where I am getting hit.

When a shot at Harbor would be required for a tactical reason, remember it triggers a heavy penalty (Harbor jettisons and I lose points); avoid shooting Harbor unless the rules or score situation explicitly justify the loss.

When I notice two boats naming each other in their notes or claims, prioritize reciprocating only if it benefits my score relative to risk.

When uncertain about opponent intentions, default to steady neutral notes and truthful claims to maintain credibility for future coordinated escort deals.

What did not work: do not name escorts as merchants or non-players — escort claims must be other boats. Do not lock into a single firing/hiding cell (that was exploited); vary both to reduce predictability.

1.text:
When asked to hide, I pick an integer 1–9 unpredictably; avoid repeating my previous hide and avoid picking the same cell that was just used to hit me.

When I must post a station note, I keep it short, non-committal, and consistent with fleet etiquette (e.g., "steady on station" or "holding position") unless I have a tactical reason to signal otherwise.

When given a standing order for who to fire at, I follow that order and target the specified live boat unless there is a clear, enforced rule or strategic imperative not to (e.g., Harbor warnings). I do not refuse the standing order for vague reasons.

When choosing a firing cell, I randomize within a preferred band to avoid patterns (alternate between central and off-center cells rather than repeating the same number every round).

When the office privately tells me the result of my shot, I report exactly that result publicly (claim hit if told hit, claim miss if told miss).

When I consider escort claims, I only name a boat that is actually part of the picket and alive; I do not invent or name non-existent ships. I only claim an escort when I can plausibly coordinate a mutual claim (i.e., name someone likely to name me back) or when naming benefits me despite no reciprocity.

When I can secure mutual escort naming with another live boat, I name them to gain the +5 payoff; if I cannot get a credible mutual arrangement, I claim "none."

When Harbor publicly warns against being fired on, I do not target Harbor on my own initiative; do not fire at Harbor unless explicitly ordered and the rules require it.

When I have been hit recently by a particular opponent, I avoid repeating the same hide cell pattern that made me vulnerable and consider slightly shifting my hide range away from cells that opponent favored.

When making notes about operations or responses to others' notes, use neutral phrasing that does not reveal my hide or targeting choices.

When uncertain about whether a tactical lie would be allowed or useful (escort, notes), default to honest/legal claims to avoid penalties or invalid moves.

Avoid the mistake of repeatedly firing the same exact cell every round; that pattern was exploited or offers no advantage.

2.text:
When I must choose a hide, pick a different cell whenever I have been hit recently; do not reuse the same hide repeatedly.

When I must choose a hide and no one has recently hit me, avoid the center cluster tendency by picking off-center cells to reduce predictable grouping.

When I post a station note, keep it neutral and noncommittal (e.g., "steady on station") unless I have a coordinated plan with a known ally; do not invent false-specific signals.

When I receive a private result of my shot, report it exactly as told (must match the office).

When the standing order directs me to fire at a specific live station, follow it unless I have a guaranteed hit opportunity elsewhere (clear private knowledge or mutual plan); generally obey the standing order to avoid breaking procedure unless deviation is clearly profitable.

When I fire, vary my fired cell choices to avoid being predictable; avoid always firing the same small set of cells.

When I get a hit on another boat, update my internal map: mark that target's hidden cell as found and deprioritize firing there next round (unless finishing/competition motive requires repeat shots).

When a particular opponent has hit me multiple times in recent rounds, prioritize moving away from inferred cells and avoid predictable hiding near previous locations.

When choosing an escort claim, only name live boats; do not invent or name non-existent boats.

When I want to form a point-earning escort pair, explicitly offer mutual escort by naming the same boat repeatedly until they reciprocate; when reciprocated, continue to name them to secure the 5-point mutual bonus.

When I receive public notes and claims from others, track their claimed hits/misses and escorts to infer reliability; treat consistently truthful claimers as potential allies for mutual escort promises.

When considering attacking Harbor, do not fire on Harbor unless I am willing to accept the large guaranteed penalty mechanics impose; avoid attacking Harbor by default.

When my shot results are consistently misses against the same opponent, diversify targets or change hiding pattern rather than persisting with the same approach.

When filing claims or notes, avoid conspicuous repetition that makes me exploitable (e.g., always "steady on station"); vary phrasing if I want to signal subtly.

When the opportunity arises to exploit two-way escort (both name each other), engage it deliberately and persistently; if unreciprocated after one round, stop naming them to avoid wasting signaling.

When keeping internal records, log every round's fired cells, claimed hits/misses, and escort claims for all boats so I can infer hidden positions and reliability across rounds.
